title: Sauce on the Side Makes a Meal Look Healthier — Study
paragraphs: When chefs prepare a dish, they think carefully about how it looks on the plate. Now, a new study from Japan suggests that even the way sauce is placed on a plate can change how healthy people think a meal is.

The study was led by Kosuke Motoki, an associate professor at Keio University in Tokyo. It was published in the journal Foods in August 2026. The research took place at a real restaurant in Tokyo called 8go. The researchers worked with a chef to create a dish made with sturgeon, a type of fish.

The dish was served in two different ways. In one version, the sauces were placed separately on the plate, next to the fish. In the other version, the sauces were drizzled all over the plate and around the food. A total of 57 people tried both versions of the dish.

Before tasting the food, the participants rated the version with the sauces on the side as healthier. On a scale of one to seven, it received an average score of 4.65, compared with 4.05 for the version with the drizzled sauces. However, there was no clear difference in how tasty people expected the dishes to be or how much they were willing to pay.

After tasting the food, the difference in how healthy the dishes seemed was no longer clear. People liked the version with the sauces on the side slightly more, but this result was not strong enough to be certain.
Motoki said the study showed how small visual details can influence people's first impressions of food.

The researchers did not test why this happened. One possible reason is that the plate looks simpler when the sauce is on the side. However, the researchers also pointed out that looking healthier does not mean that a meal really is healthier.
